passages.title: A Visit to the Local Museum
passages.text:
On Thursday, thirty pupils from Riverbank School visited a small local museum. Before leaving, their teacher, Mr Sen, divided them into five groups. Each group received a different question to investigate. His purpose was to help everyone look closely instead of simply copying labels.

At the entrance, a guide explained two rules: visitors must not touch the objects, and they should speak quietly. Sami was interested in an old wooden boat. He first thought it was a toy, but the label said that fishers had used it on a nearby river. The guide explained that the river had once been an important route for travel and trade.

In another room, the pupils saw a display of woven baskets. There was no date on one label. Rather than guessing, Liza wrote, "Date not given," in her notebook and prepared a question for the guide. The guide promised to check the museum records; she did not provide a date immediately.

Back at school, each group presented one finding and one unanswered question. The class learned that a good visitor notices details, respects shared objects and admits when information is missing.

activities.instruction: Summarise the main events and lesson of P1 in your own words. No official word limit is asserted.
activities.modelAnswer: Pupils visited a local museum in groups to investigate different questions. They followed the museum rules and used labels and a guide to understand the objects. When information was missing, they recorded a question instead of guessing. Their reports showed the value of careful observation, respect and honest inquiry.

activities.instruction: Put these sentences in order using the time and reference clues.

sentences.A: With the timetable checked, she chose a suitable morning service.
sentences.B: After choosing the service, she asked her father to book the tickets.
sentences.C: The following morning, the family reached the station with those tickets.
sentences.D: First, Nila checked the train timetable for her family trip.
sentences.E: Once seated on the train, they put their bags safely beside them.
sentences.F: When their train arrived, they boarded it and found their seats.
sentences.G: After settling their bags, they watched the train leave the platform.

activities.instruction: Complete this story: During a school exhibition, Adil noticed that a label had fallen from a display. He was about to put it beside an object when he realised ...
activities.modelAnswer: Adil realised that he did not know which object the label belonged to. Two models stood close together, and either one might have been the right choice. He left the label on a clear table and told the teacher in charge. Together, they checked the list of exhibits prepared by the pupils. The list showed that the label belonged to a small model bridge, not the house beside it. The teacher helped Adil put it back in the correct place. Later, a visitor used the label to understand how the bridge had been built. Adil was glad that he had asked instead of guessing. He learned that even a small mistake can confuse other people, and that checking information is worth the time.
assessment: Shows a clear problem and a plausible resolution
Uses relevant detail without an unrelated ending

activities.instruction: Write a paragraph on how to be a responsible visitor to a public place.
activities.modelAnswer: A responsible visitor enjoys a public place without making it difficult for others to enjoy it. Before a visit, we should learn the basic rules and ask an adult if anything is unclear. In a museum, we should not touch objects unless a sign or guide allows it. Speaking quietly helps other visitors listen and think. In a park, we can use the paths, protect plants and put our rubbish in a suitable bin. If there is no bin nearby, we can keep safe rubbish in a bag until we find one. We should also respect queues and leave space for people who need it. When we have a question, asking politely is better than making a careless guess or disturbing a display. Public places belong to a wider community, so our actions should show care for both people and shared resources.
assessment: Maintains the topic of responsible visiting
Uses clear sentences and appropriate vocabulary

activities.instruction: Write a dialogue between a pupil and a museum guide about an object with an incomplete label.

modelAnswer.speaker: Pupil
modelAnswer.line: Excuse me, may I ask about this basket?

modelAnswer.speaker: Guide
modelAnswer.line: Of course. What would you like to know?

modelAnswer.speaker: Pupil
modelAnswer.line: The label describes its use, but I cannot find a date. When was it made?

modelAnswer.speaker: Guide
modelAnswer.line: I do not have a confirmed date at the moment.

modelAnswer.speaker: Pupil
modelAnswer.line: Should I write an approximate year in my notebook?

modelAnswer.speaker: Guide
modelAnswer.line: Please write that the date is not given. We should not guess.

modelAnswer.speaker: Pupil
modelAnswer.line: Is there another source we could check?

modelAnswer.speaker: Guide
modelAnswer.line: I can check the museum records and ask the curator.

modelAnswer.speaker: Pupil
modelAnswer.line: Thank you. I will keep the question in my notes.

modelAnswer.speaker: Guide
modelAnswer.line: You are welcome. Asking careful questions is part of learning.

assessment: Has a relevant exchange of questions and responses
